summary: The main article describes a photo-induced, oxidant-free C-H/N-H cross-coupling method using a dual photocatalyst/cobalt system. It includes 2 tables for optimization and oxidant comparison, 3 figures detailing substrate scope and mechanistic studies, and 1 scheme illustrating the proposed reaction mechanism.

items.heading: Figure 1
items.caption: Reaction design. ( a ) Important molecules containing N -arylzoles moiety. ( b ) Amination of benzylic C-H bond by Zhu and co-workers 23 . ( c ) The C(sp 2 )-H amination of methylarenes under oxidant-free conditions.
items.description: This figure contrasts previous benzylic C-H amination methods with the current work's selective aromatic C(sp2)-H amination approach.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Investigation of reaction conditions.
items.description: Optimization table showing the screening of various photocatalysts and co-catalysts for the coupling of p-xylene and pyrazole.

items.heading: Table 2
items.caption: Comparison of oxidant-free system and photocatalyst/oxidant system.
items.description: This table compares the efficiency of the oxidant-free cobalt system against various traditional chemical oxidants.

items.heading: Figure 2
items.caption: Substrate scope of arenes 1 with azoles 2.
items.description: Displays the variety of methylarenes and azoles compatible with the reaction conditions and their resulting yields.

items.heading: Figure 3
items.caption: Substrate scope of pyrazole 2a with other aromatic arenes 4.
items.description: Shows the expansion of the reaction scope to other aromatic systems like biphenyl, anisole, and dihydrocoumarin.

items.heading: Figure 4
items.caption: Investigation for mechanistic insights. ( a ) The intermolecular kinetic of isotopic effect experiment. ( b ) Kinetic plots of the reactions with different concentrations of biphenyl 4a.
items.description: Presents kinetic data including KIE results and reaction order plots to support the proposed mechanism.

items.heading: Figure 5
items.caption: Proposed mechanism for oxidant-free C-H amination.
items.description: A catalytic cycle illustrating the synergistic roles of the acridinium photocatalyst and the cobalt co-catalyst in generating H2 and the C-N coupled product.
